# Lab 18.5: Column-Level Security with Policy Tags

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a policy tag taxonomy, tag the email column as PII, and allow only selected users to read it.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create the taxonomy and a policy tag.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable datacatalog.googleapis.com
gcloud data-catalog taxonomies create --location=us --display-name="Sensitivity" \
  --activated-policy-types=FINE_GRAINED_ACCESS_CONTROL
TAX=$(gcloud data-catalog taxonomies list --location=us --format="value(name)" --filter="displayName=Sensitivity")
gcloud data-catalog taxonomies policy-tags create --taxonomy=$TAX --location=us --display-name="PII"
TAG=$(gcloud data-catalog taxonomies policy-tags list --taxonomy=$TAX --location=us --format="value(name)")
echo $TAG</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Tag the column.** Open `lab18_private.users → Schema → Edit schema`. Tick `email`, click **Add policy tag**, choose **Sensitivity → PII**. Save.

3. **[CLI] Or tag it with a schema file.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq show --schema --format=prettyjson lab18_private.users &gt; users_schema.json
python3 - &lt;&lt;EOF
import json
s = json.load(open("users_schema.json"))
for f in s:
    if f["name"] == "email":
        f["policyTags"] = {"names": ["$TAG"]}
json.dump(s, open("users_schema.json", "w"))
EOF
bq update lab18_private.users users_schema.json</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Test.** Run `SELECT email FROM lab18_private.users LIMIT 5;`. You get **Access Denied** even as the owner. Run `SELECT * EXCEPT (email) …` and it works.

5. **[CLI] Grant Fine-Grained Reader.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud data-catalog taxonomies policy-tags add-iam-policy-binding $TAG --taxonomy=$TAX --location=us \
  --member="user:$(gcloud config get-value account)" --role=roles/datacatalog.categoryFineGrainedReader</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Now you can read `email`.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Taxonomy | Hierarchy of policy tags |
| Tagged column | Blocked unless you are a Fine-Grained Reader |
| Owners | Also blocked without the role |
| Other columns | Unaffected |
